findings.title: [P3] When `maxLen` is below `suffix.length`, omitted, or non-numeric, the result is longer than `maxLen`
findings.body: `str.slice(0, maxLen - suffix.length) + suffix` uses a negative slice end when `maxLen < suffix.length`, so `truncate("hello", 2)` returns `"hell..."` (length 7, longer than both `maxLen` and nothing was really truncated), and `truncate("hello")`, `truncate("hello", NaN)`, `truncate("hello", -3)` all return `"..."` because `str.length <= maxLen` is false for NaN. This is outside the literal contract rather than a violation of it: the objective specifies behavior only for `str.length <= maxLen` and for the shortening case, and in the sub-suffix region no return value can satisfy "total length including suffix equals maxLen". Surfaced as an observation for whoever promotes this utility beyond the example; not a follow-up requirement for this run.
